answer: Each identity may bind only one hardware authenticator, and a credential already registered to one name is refused for any other. Each epoch the network issues a one-time challenge that must be signed on that same device within a short window; missed or replayed assertions earn no weight. That credential is a scarce pigment: it can mark only a single jade identity. An umber mass of look-alike names still requires a distinct, live authenticator for each, so a farm's cost scales with physical devices kept ready every epoch.
